title: Lane X2: Internal Rigged Local Runtime Architecture — OMLX-Informed, MLX-Backed Production Boundary
summary: Product owner has corrected the mission: OMLX is not merely an external endpoint to tolerate, nor is its MLX dependency tree prohibited. OMLX is an Apache-2.0 reference implementation and legitimate adaptation source for a Rig-governed internal local runtime. This decision separates the runtime into five categories: (1) Rig Relay internally implements using OMLX as a reference (model loading via mlx-lm, governed text inference, typed evidence pipeline, model inventory from local filesystem); (2) Rig Relay adapts from OMLX under Apache 2.0 (model classification taxonomy, cache evidence metrics schema, capability probe structure); (3) Rig Relay consumes through MLX ecosystem directly (mlx-lm for generation, mlx for GPU operations, transformers for tokenization); (4) OMLX mechanisms deferred (continuous batching scheduler, tiered KV cache, prefix sharing, engine pool, VLM/OCR pipeline); (5) Capabilities excluded from current slice (embeddings/reranking/VLM live integration, benchmark integration, streaming governance). Nine new production dependencies introduced under justified Apache 2.0 adaptation: mlx, mlx-lm, transformers, tokenizers, huggingface-hub, numpy, protobuf, sentencepiece, tiktoken. The implementation is an internal MLX-backed runtime called RiggedLocalRuntime — a typed application-service boundary that loads models and performs inference through mlx-lm APIs under Rig Relay governance, preserving absolute authority over privacy, task admission, tool execution, evidence, and UI projection.

key_facts: OMLX is Apache 2.0 (no NOTICE file). Copyright: oMLX contributors (2025).

Full-source inspection verified: 15 API endpoints, continuous batching scheduler (6,596 lines), tiered KV cache (6,000+ lines across 16 files), engine pool (1,020 lines), 11 engine types, 84 admin routes.
Core inference library: mlx-lm provides Python APIs (load, generate, stream_generate) that are directly consumable — no OMLX server code needed.
MLX ecosystem is Apple Silicon only, all dependencies are permissively licensed (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD, HPND).
model_registry.py (191 lines): weakref-based singleton for tracking model ownership — informs our inventory approach.
model_discovery.py (909 lines): config.json inspection, model_type+architecture detection, safetensors size estimation — informs our inventory scanner.

alternatives.name: External Runtime Integration (W0 — REJECTED)
alternatives.description: Rig Relay connects to a separately installed OMLX server via HTTP adapter.
alternatives.rejection_rationale: Insuffizient. Does not create a Rig-owned runtime. Surrenders local-runtime product surface to unmanaged external application.

alternatives.name: Internal MLX-Backed Governed Runtime (X2 selected)
alternatives.description: Rig Relay implements an internal runtime using mlx-lm APIs directly for model loading and inference, wrapped in Rig Relay's governance boundary (admission, privacy, evidence, tool authority). OMLX is the reference implementation and adaptation source.

alternatives.name: Full OMLX Engine Port
alternatives.description: Adapt OMLX's entire engine/scheduler/cache stack (15,000+ lines) into Rig Relay.
alternatives.rejection_rationale: Massive scope. OMLX's scheduler (6,596 lines) and cache (6,000+ lines) are tightly coupled to MLX GPU memory management, Metal buffer pools, and specific git commit pins. Porting the full stack would require months. The mlx-lm library already provides clean Python APIs for the core inference path — building on those is faster and more maintainable.

selected_direction.name: Internal MLX-Backed Governed Runtime
selected_direction.rationale: This is the first real internal Rig Relay runtime. It uses mlx-lm APIs directly for model loading and inference, wrapped in Rig Relay's governance boundary. It does NOT require OMLX's server, scheduler, or cache code — mlx-lm.load() and mlx-lm.generate() provide the core inference capability. The governance boundary (admission, privacy, evidence, tool authority) is 100% Rig Relay. OMLX is the Apache-2.0 reference that informed the architecture pattern, model classification taxonomy, and evidence schema shapes.

category_2_adapted_from_omlx_apache2: Model classification taxonomy: OMLX's model_discovery.py architecture detection (VLM via config.json architectures, embedding via model class names, reranker via CausalLM heuristic) informs ModelInventoryEntry.model_type. Attribution in _models.py.
Cache evidence metrics schema: OMLX's CacheRateTracker rolling window pattern (60s, 5m, 15m) informs CacheEvidenceMetrics. Attribution in _models.py.
Capability probe structure: OMLX's endpoint layout (/health, /v1/models, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank, /api/status) informs EnrichedRuntimeCapabilities. Attribution in _models.py.
mlx-lm thread-local stream pattern: OMLX's engine_core.py (lines 35-61, _init_mlx_thread) informs MLX execution thread safety. Adaptation noted in _engine.py.

mlx-lm ~ language model library (MIT) — load(), generate(), stream_generate()

Admin panel: 84 routes for model management, settings, downloads — UI surface outside X2 scope

dependencies_added.justification: Nine dependencies added to enable MLX-backed internal runtime under Rig Relay governance. All are permissively licensed (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD, HPND). None are copyleft. All are production dependencies of mlx-lm, the core inference library that provides Python APIs for model loading and generation.

adapted_patterns_from_omlx.rationale: mlx-lm uses a module-level Metal stream that must be initialized on the correct thread. OMLX's pattern of creating a thread-local stream and replacing the module-level reference is the safe approach. Adapted as a pattern reference.

licensing_assessment.model_license_separation: Apache 2.0 covers MLX ecosystem application code only. MLX-lm models downloaded from HuggingFace carry their own licenses (LLaMA Community, Mistral Research, DeepSeek, etc.). Rig Relay never implies MLX ecosystem licenses extend to model weights. Users are solely responsible for model license compliance.
licensing_assessment.rig_relay_license: AGPL-3.0-or-later. All added dependencies are permissively licensed and compatible. No copyleft dependencies.

cache_privacy_rules.local_kv_cache_is_not_cloud_retention: Per W1 Principle 4: MLX local KV cache is modeled as local-runtime performance evidence, not as cloud retention. Local inference data never leaves the machine.
cache_privacy_rules.mlx_in_process_cache_behavior: mlx-lm.generate() uses in-memory KV cache that is not persisted across calls. This provides the strongest privacy guarantee — no persistent cache to inspect or manage.
cache_privacy_rules.future_persistent_cache: If persistent SSD KV cache is implemented later (OMLX-informed), it must follow the existing cache privacy contract: disclosure required, content-light evidence only, never read cache contents.
cache_privacy_rules.content_light_cache_evidence: Rig Relay records cache capability status and policy as content-light evidence. Never records raw prompt text, generated text, or model output in cache evidence.

tool_authority_rule.runtime_output_is_proposal_only: Model-generated text containing tool-call-formatted output is recorded as proposed model output only. It routes through existing Rig Relay governed execution/application-service authority.
tool_authority_rule.no_direct_execution_path: No code path allows model output to directly execute tools, mutate files, or change repository state.
tool_authority_rule.tests_required: Tests must prove that model tool-call output cannot bypass governed execution.

released_boundary: RiggedLocalRuntimeBoundary: an internal MLX-backed governed local inference runtime, informed by and legally compatible with OMLX's Apache-2.0 reference architecture, that preserves Rig Relay authority over privacy, task admission, tool execution, evidence, and UI projection while providing real model loading, governed inference, model inventory, and typed execution evidence for future Inference Studio consumption.
stated_consumer_purpose: A later X0/X2 integration milestone wires Inference Studio to a real Rig-governed local runtime (MLX-backed model loading and inference under Rig admission/evidence/tool authority) rather than an external endpoint placeholder.
deferred_seams: Continuous batching (single-request inference only; scheduler engine requires separate implementation slice)
KV cache persistence (in-memory only; SSD safetensors cache requires separate implementation slice)
Prefix sharing and cache reuse across requests
Multi-model serving and engine pool lifecycle
VLM/OCR live integration (requires mlx-vlm, Pillow dependencies)
Streaming inference with per-token governance and token budgeting
Real model inference on CI (requires Apple Silicon hardware)
freeze_condition: This lane freezes upon remote verification of published architecture decision, implementation, tests, dependency changes, and license compliance artifacts. Reopens only for: a concrete defect inside the released boundary, a named X0/X2 integration milestone consuming this boundary, or a user-directed architectural revision.
